# Incident Report — Network Traffic Analysis
**Source evidence:** `2022-01-07-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (5,880 packets, capture window 2022-01-07 20:04:09–20:16:40 local), plus pre-extracted HTTP objects in `exported_objects/`. No Suricata/IDS alert export was present in the evidence directory; findings below are derived directly from packet analysis via tshark.

## 1. Victim Host

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | 192.168.1.216 |
| MAC address | 9c:5c:8e:32:58:f9 |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-GXMYNO2 (confirmed via DHCP option 12, mDNS, LLMNR, and Kerberos `desktop-gxmyno2$`) |
| AD domain | SPOONWATCH.NET (DC: SPOONWATCH-DC / 192.168.1.2) |
| Logged-in Windows user | **steve.smith** (Kerberos AS-REQ `CNameString: steve.smith`, realm SPOONWATCH.NET/SPOONWATCH) |

The capture opens with the host's DHCP lease (frame 1) and domain-join chatter (LDAP/CLDAP/Kerberos to the DC), then C2 activity begins only ~3 minutes after boot — consistent with a malicious binary already resident on disk running at logon/startup, not a fresh drive-by in this capture. No initial infection vector (phishing email, exploit, malicious document/LNK download) appears in this pcap; the capture only covers a post-compromise C2 check-in.

## 2. Malware Family

**Behaviorally consistent with an information-stealer of the Vidar/Arkei family.** Attribution is **behavioral, not signature-confirmed** — no AV/IDS detection artifact was included in the evidence, so this is based on TTP fingerprinting, not a rule hit.

Basis for the assessment:
- A single ~4-second HTTP session (TCP stream 65) to a **hardcoded IP with no preceding DNS lookup** — client went straight to `2.56.57.108` without ever resolving a name for it.
- Client sent **no `User-Agent` header**, used `Accept-Language: ru-RU,ru;q=0.9,en;q=0.8`, and reused a **static multipart boundary** (`1BEF0A57BE110FD467A`) across every request — not a real browser fingerprint.
- The client downloaded a bundle of **7 files disguised as `.jpg` (Content-Type: image/jpeg) that are actually Win32 PE DLLs**: `sqlite3.dll`, `freebl3.dll`, `nss3.dll`, `mozglue.dll`, `softokn3.dll`, `msvcp140.dll`, `vcruntime140.dll`. This exact legitimate-Mozilla-NSS/runtime DLL set is the well-known dependency bundle stealers use to open and decrypt Firefox/Chromium SQLite credential/cookie stores locally on the victim (rather than exfiltrating raw encrypted DBs).
- Immediately after, the malware **exfiltrated a ZIP archive** (`_5861695120.zip`) via POST to the same server, containing files under an `autofill/` folder (`Google Chrome_Default.txt`, `Microsoft Edge_Default...`) — harvested browser autofill data.

This "fetch NSS/SQLite DLLs → parse local browser stores → zip and POST results" workflow is the textbook Vidar/Arkei-style stealer pattern.

## 3. Indicators of Compromise

### Command-and-control
- **C2 endpoint:** `2.56.57.108:80/tcp` (HTTP, plaintext, no TLS)
- **Malicious domains:** none observed — C2 was reached by hardcoded IP address only, no DNS query for it exists in the capture.

### Malicious URLs (all POST, TCP stream 65, 20:07:32–20:07:36 local)
| URL | Purpose | Response |
|---|---|---|
| `http://2.56.57.108/osk//1.jpg` | Downloaded module (PE32 DLL, console) | 200, `image/jpeg` (fake) |
| `http://2.56.57.108/osk//2.jpg` | Downloaded module (PE32 DLL, GUI) | 200, `image/jpeg` (fake) |
| `http://2.56.57.108/osk//3.jpg` | Downloaded module (PE32 DLL, GUI) | 200, `image/jpeg` (fake) |
| `http://2.56.57.108/osk//4.jpg` | Downloaded module (PE32 DLL, console) | 200, `image/jpeg` (fake) |
| `http://2.56.57.108/osk//5.jpg` | Downloaded module (PE32 DLL, GUI) | 200, `image/jpeg` (fake) |
| `http://2.56.57.108/osk//6.jpg` | Downloaded module (PE32 DLL, GUI) | 200, `image/jpeg` (fake) |
| `http://2.56.57.108/osk//7.jpg` | Downloaded module (PE32 DLL, console) | 200, `image/jpeg` (fake) |
| `http://2.56.57.108/osk//main.php` | Gate/check-in call | 200, empty body |
| `http://2.56.57.108/osk/` | **Data exfiltration** — POST of `_5861695120.zip` (harvested browser autofill data) | 200 |

### Transferred files and SHA-256 hashes (from exported HTTP objects)
| File (as served/named) | True type | SHA-256 |
|---|---|---|
| `1.jpg` | PE32 DLL — bundles `sqlite3` | `16574f51785b0e2fc29c2c61477eb47bb39f714829999511dc8952b43ab17660` |
| `2.jpg` | PE32 DLL — `freebl3.dll`/`nss3.dll` | `a770ecba3b08bbabd0a567fc978e50615f8b346709f8eb3cfacf3faab24090ba` |
| `3.jpg` | PE32 DLL — `mozglue.dll` | `3fe6b1c54b8cf28f571e0c5d6636b4069a8ab00b4f11dd842cfec00691d0c9cd` |
| `4.jpg` | PE32 DLL — `msvcp140.dll` | `334e69ac9367f708ce601a6f490ff227d6c20636da5222f148b25831d22e13d4` |
| `5.jpg` | PE32 DLL — SQLite DB engine | `e2935b5b28550d47dc971f456d6961f20d1633b4892998750140e0eaa9ae9d78` |
| `6.jpg` | PE32 DLL — `freebl3.dll`/`softokn3.dll` | `43536adef2ddcc811c28d35fa6ce3031029a2424ad393989db36169ff2995083` |
| `7.jpg` | PE32 DLL — `vcruntime140.dll` | `c40bb03199a2054dabfc7a8e01d6098e91de7193619effbd0f142a7bf031c14d` |
| `_5861695120.zip` (exfil upload body, captured to `osk`) | ZIP archive, browser `autofill/` data (Chrome, Edge) | `1ecee6ff37e03c1160b8bf66d5ca8dc784e0b35fb9fd105f0964b314d310c07f` (of the captured multipart upload as saved) |

### Not malicious (ruled out during analysis)
Traffic to `download.windowsupdate.com`, `au.download.windowsupdate.com`, `ctldl.windowsupdate.com` (Akamai IPs `23.38.189.225`, `23.38.189.201`, `8.253.189.126`) delivering `.cab` files and `am_delta_patch_1.355.1569.0...exe` is legitimate Windows Defender definition-update traffic, unrelated to the intrusion.

## 4. Summary
Host **DESKTOP-GXMYNO2** (192.168.1.216, MAC 9c:5c:8e:32:58:f9), logged in as domain user **steve.smith** (SPOONWATCH.NET), phoned home to a hardcoded C2 at **2.56.57.108:80**, pulled down a 7-DLL toolkit disguised as JPEG images to locally decrypt stored Chromium/Firefox browser data, and exfiltrated a ZIP of harvested browser autofill data — behavior consistent with a **Vidar/Arkei-family information stealer** (behavioral attribution; no signature/AV detection artifact was present in the supplied evidence to confirm the exact family/build).
